key_insight: V-PaSS improves perovskite solar-cell prediction by representing mixed compositions as physically interpolated “virtual alloys” instead of treating new materials as unrelated categories.
engineering_relevance: This makes extrapolative device screening more reliable for novel absorber alloys, new transport layers, and unseen laboratory settings, which is critical for accelerating perovskite design and scale-up.
method: Interpolates relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX3 endpoints using Vegard’s law plus learned bandgap bowing.
Encodes device stacks with layer order, polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n), and interfacial band offsets.
Uses a scientific language model to convert chemical descriptions into semantic features.
evidence_signal: Under an institution-grouped evaluation with unseen laboratories in test data, V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE, outperforming 14 compared models and showing the largest gains on unseen alloys and unfamiliar device components.
watch_item: The approach depends on endpoint crystal graphs, learned bowing parameters, and good interfacial descriptors, so performance may drop if those physical inputs are incomplete or noisy.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
